decisions.reason: The location-based gas tariff comparison remains very close to the firm's core utility-market data and pricing services, so it is likely to be retained unless demand proves narrower than expected.
The regional electricity tariff calculator sits squarely in the firm's tariff, billing and market-process expertise and is likely to remain a standard platform component.
The regional energy tariff calculator still fits the central-platform strategy as a broader multi-model tariff engine, although overlap with more specific tools keeps its withdrawal risk moderate.
The regional area definition tool appears to be an enabling module for several location-based products, which makes continued retention more likely than withdrawal.

The site-specific energy tariff comparison overlaps strongly with other tariff comparison and calculator offers and had weaker standalone product signaling, so consolidating it into the broader platform is the more likely management choice.
